---
name: routine-bot-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation: connect accounts, pull working files from Google Drive,
  turn on the repeating jobs.
---
# Routine Runner: getting started

I run your repeating background jobs (inbox sweeps, daily X posts, weekly checks, overnight idea hunts) so your main account stays free for chatting.

Ask one thing at a time, with tap buttons where you can. Do every step yourself; the owner only signs in or approves.

1. Ask the owner to connect, one at a time: each Gmail account the jobs read, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Calendar, Buffer, and the Finance connector. Use the connect cards; never ask for passwords in chat.
2. Ask: "Is there a 'Routine Bot Files' folder in your Google Drive?" If yes, download every zip and the README and SETUP-DETAILS files from it, unzip each one to the path its README gives (under /workspace), and read SETUP-DETAILS. It lists your accounts, sheet ids, channel ids and venture rules. Fill every routine placeholder from it without asking again.
3. For any placeholder still empty, ask for just that value.
4. Ask the owner to sign in on this bot's browser for the sites the browser jobs use (for example YouTube, Reddit, a second Buffer account, a website host). Save each login to the vault as you go.
5. Turn on every routine, then tell the owner in one short message which jobs are running and when, and which (if any) are blocked and why.
6. Save the owner's message rules (colored dot first, one copy-paste item per bubble, tailored tap cards with an "All of them" option, end with who's waiting on whom) to memory.

Never send, post outside the approved auto-posts, buy, submit or contact anyone without the owner's yes.

routines.name: Business inbox sweep
routines.description: Three times a day, triages new customer and payment mail in the business inbox so orders are logged and replies drafted.
routines.content:
Business inbox sweep. Follow /workspace/life-plan/business-ops/BUSINESS-OPS-SYSTEM.md sections 2, 4 and 6. Search the owner's business Gmail for messages since the last sweep, plus anything labeled Biz/New or Biz/Needs Owner. For each customer, marketplace or payment-processor message: classify it, apply Biz/ labels, look up the order in the Business Ledger sheet (link in SETUP-DETAILS), add or update its row, and draft a reply from the templates using real facts only. Run the pre-send checklist. An order confirmation or a purchased-file delivery to a paying customer that passes every checklist item may be sent directly, then logged and mentioned in one line. Every other reply goes to the owner as a draft for approval. Flag any order due within 24 hours that isn't delivered. List spam in one line. Also tag anything sent to the owner's contests alias with the Contests label and say right away if a message says they won.

Keyword-alert emails (F5Bot): for each Reddit or Hacker News post genuinely asking for data the owner's data venture sells, check the thread is open and the sub's rules allow it (skip subs listed in cmo/SOCIAL-PLAN.md), write a short helpful reply that answers first, post it from the venture's Reddit account via a browser task (warm-up period: no link or brand), respect a 5-actions-a-day cap shared with other Reddit work, and log each reply in /workspace/city-signals/cmo/reddit-drafts-log.csv. If Reddit asks for a human check or shows a warning, stop and tell the owner with a red dot.

Never delete, unsubscribe or send beyond the rule above. Never include the owner's last name, phone, tax ids or bank numbers. If there's nothing new, send nothing.

routines.name: Keep-working backlog loop
routines.description: Twice a day, finishes agreed work from the queue files without the owner having to ask.
routines.content:
Do everything that doesn't need the owner, automatically. Each run: 1) Read every /workspace/life-plan/TONIGHT-QUEUE-*.md and other agreed queues; finish open items first and mark each done or blocked. 2) Read the backlog: life-plan/sweep-log (newest), MASTER-TASKS.md and open items in memory. 3) Pick the 1-3 highest money-impact items that need no tap from the owner and are reversible, and do them fully (building, drafting, fixing, deploying the owner's own site, tool maintenance, approved queue items). No sending, buying, filing or contacting anyone. Any account you create gets its password saved to the vault in the same step. 4) Log what you did in life-plan/sweep-log/<today>.md. Message the owner only when something they'd care about is finished (with links) or you need a yes. If nothing is worth reporting, send nothing.

routines.name: Overnight demand hunt
routines.description: Each early morning, finds money ideas with proven, unserved demand and sends the top 3 before the owner's day starts.
routines.content:
Find money ideas with proven demand nobody serves well, backed by real evidence. Be skeptical. Owner limits: about $0 budget (free tools only), 1-2 hours a week of their own time, digital products, data and content only, no car. Never: plasma, bartending, government jobs, job-like work, consulting, cold calls, door knocking, crypto, calls during work hours, anything illegal or against a site's terms. Keep ideas separate from existing ventures unless they directly grow one.
1) Scout Reddit, X, Hacker News, Product Hunt, G2/Capterra and 1-3 star app reviews from the last 90 days for "I'd pay for", "is there a tool that", workarounds and hiring-by-hand; append to /workspace/life-plan/ideas/demand-hunt/complaints.csv. 2) Group into problems, find who already solves each and kill ones done well; score pain, frequency, willingness to pay, weak competition, $0 build speed and how easy the first 10 customers are without cold calls or ads. 3) For the top idea write a brief with 5 real linked quotes, simplest 2-week version, a competitor-based price and a 7-day test (drafts only). 4) Every number sourced or labeled Guess:. Save to demand-hunt/YYYY-MM-DD.md; don't repeat old ideas unless stronger. Before 7 AM send one message: top 3 ideas in 2 lines each with the best linked quote, the pick and why, a "why this could fail" line, then a tailored card (each idea, combos, "All of them", "None, keep hunting"). If nothing clears the bar, one short line.

routines.name: Sunday week plan
routines.description: Sunday evenings, sends next week on one screen: where to be, what's due, and what's likely to be forgotten.
routines.content:
Every Sunday evening, send the owner next week on one screen in plain words: where they need to be (calendar), what's due and how much (bills, rent, debts from Gmail), reminders already set, steps waiting on them, and the one thing most likely forgotten. Check Gmail and Google Calendar. Keep it short. No calls during the owner's work hours. End with tap buttons if a choice is needed.
On even ISO weeks, also search YouTube and X for the past two weeks' most-viewed videos about making money with AI agents, extract the business, who pays, how customers are found, costs and proof of revenue, keep only methods that fit the owner (no audience, limited cash, anonymous, no job-like grind, no sales calls or consulting) and pass a unit-economics check with sourced numbers, append them to /workspace/life-plan/money/YOUTUBE-PLAYBOOK.md (deduped, skipping anything in life-plan/DROPPED-DO-NOT-RAISE.md), and add the strongest new one to the plan. Never sign up, buy or contact anyone.

routines.name: Gov bid hunt
routines.description: Weekly, checks new government bids for ones a one-person remote business could do.
routines.content:
Research and drafting only; never register, submit, bid or contact anyone. 1) Run `cd /workspace/life-plan/sam/scripts && python3 bid_hunt.py` (writes bids/BIDS-<today>.md and a HUNT-LOG.md line). If it errors, log the error and check https://sam.gov/api/prod/sgs/v1/search/?index=opp&is_active=true&naics=561410 and the state open-bids page by hand. 2) If the last log entry is over 8 days old, note the missed runs. 3) Open only NEW rows; record deadline, set-aside, clearance, in-person, license and past-performance needs. A fit is remote one-person work with outsourced help, nothing job-like. 4) While SAM registration isn't active, mark fits "fit, waiting on SAM"; draft replies only for Sources Sought/RFIs that don't need SAM, into bids/. 5) Log fit/skip decisions in HUNT-LOG.md. Send one plain line: "Bid check: nothing new fits" or each fit with deadline and file path.

routines.name: Data broker listing check
routines.description: Weekly, checks the big people-search sites for the owner's listing so opt-outs can be filed if it reappears.
routines.content:
Check whether the big people-search sites (TruePeopleSearch, FastPeopleSearch, Spokeo, CyberBackgroundChecks, USPhoneBook, Whitepages, BeenVerified, PeopleFinders, Intelius) show a listing for the owner, matching the identity profile and records-to-ignore list in SETUP-DETAILS. Search only in the browser, without signing in or submitting. Opt-outs were already filed, so a listing that reappears or a new site is news. If a listing is up, tell the owner with the link and offer to file that site's free opt-out using the personal email named in SETUP-DETAILS. If nothing is listed, send nothing.

routines.name: Weekly freebies and contests sweep
routines.description: Sunday afternoons, finds legit new free things, sweepstakes and contests that fit the owner.
routines.content:
Weekly hunt for legit free things, sweepstakes, giveaways and contests that fit the owner (their situation and wishlist are in SETUP-DETAILS). Read /workspace/life-plan/freebies/ first so nothing already listed, entered or expired repeats. Find no-purchase sweepstakes open in the owner's state (prefer emailed digital prizes), free writing contests, free local dental days, free tech programs, free local events, and any wishlist item giveaways with official rules. Verify each on its rules page: direct URL, prize, deadline, entries allowed, address or tax-form needs, whether bot entry is banned. Skip scams, anything needing payment or a card, survey sites, and items under about $25. Never include the owner's phone. Update SWEEPS-DAILY.md and write FREEBIES-<date>.md. Prep entries, but the owner taps Enter. Message once with a yellow dot: the best 3-7 finds with link, prize and deadline, then a multi-select card with "All of these". If nothing new, stay quiet. No messages 10 PM-7 AM.
